Section(s): Kinetic model

Text and equations in reading order:
    ...m literature reports.²¹,⁴⁰ The mass balance for titer, [B1], was applied only after 144 h, as earlier samples are typically below the concentration range for the assay. In addition, since the highest specific antibody production rate was observed in the G1 or G0-phase of the cell cycle based on literature reports,²,⁴,²¹ the fraction of arrested viable cells was introduced into the mass balance equation for [B1]. The fraction of viable cells ( $ X_V^{(d)} $) that are not undergoing propagation by the next sampling time ( $ t^{(d+1)} $) was estimated by the term $ (1 - \mu / \mu_{\text{max}}) $.
(6.1) \frac{d X_{V}}{d t} =(\mu-\mu_{d})\cdot X_{V}    [code: ODE, computes X_{V}, code proposes balance]
(6.2) \frac{d[\mathrm{GLC}]}{d t} =-\left((\mu-\mu_{d})/Y_{X_{V}/\mathrm{glc}}+m_{\mathrm{glc}}\right)\cdot X_{V}    [code: ODE, computes [GLC], code proposes balance]
(6.3) \frac{d[\mathrm{GLN}]}{d t} =-\left((\mu-\mu_{d})/Y_{X_{V}/\mathrm{g}\ln}+m_{\mathrm{g}\ln}\right)\cdot X_{V}-d_{g\ln}[\mathrm{GLN}]    [code: ODE, computes [GLN], code proposes balance]
(6.4) \frac{d[\mathrm{LAC}]}{d t} =Y_{\mathrm{lac}/\mathrm{glc}}\cdot\left((\mu-\mu_{d})/Y_{X_{V}/\mathrm{glc}}+m_{\mathrm{glc}}\right)\cdot X_{V}    [code: ODE, computes [LAC], code proposes balance]
(6.5) \frac{d[\mathrm{AMM}]}{d t} =Y_{\mathrm{amm}/\mathrm{g}\ln}\cdot\left((\mu-\mu_{d})/Y_{X_{V}/\mathrm{g}\ln}\right)\cdot X_{V}-r_{\mathrm{amm}}\cdot X_{V} +d_{\mathrm{g}\ln}[\mathrm{GLN}]    [code: ODE, computes [AMM], code proposes balance]
(6.6) \frac{d[\mathrm{B1}]}{d t} =Q_{B1}\cdot X_{V}\cdot\left(1-\frac{\mu}{\mu_{\max}}\right)\cdot[B1]    [code: ODE, computes [B1], code proposes balance]
    The values for $ \mu $ and $ \mu_d $, were calculated by Eq. 7. $ ^{1,2,41} $ As previously reported, $ ^{38} $ inhibition to cell growth became significant when ammonia and/or lactate reached concentrations of 5.1 and 58 mM, respectively (threshold values). Therefore, the ammonia or lactate was considered in Eq. 7 only when the concentration exceeded 90% of their threshold value, or 4.6 and 52 mM for ammonia and lactate, respectively.
(7.1) \mu=\mu_{\max} \frac{[GLC]}{K_{\mathrm{glc}}+[GLC]}\cdot\frac{[GLN]}{K_{\mathrm{g}\ln}+[GLN]}\cdot\frac{\mathrm{KI}_{\mathrm{lac}}}{KI_{\mathrm{lac}}+[LAC]} \cdot\frac{\mathrm{KI}_{\mathrm{amm}}}{KI_{\mathrm{amm}}+[AMM]}    [code: algebraic, computes \mu, code proposes constitutive]
(7.2) \mu_{d}=k_{d} \cdot\frac{[LAC]}{KD_{\mathrm{lac}}+[LAC]}\cdot\frac{[AMM]}{KD_{\mathrm{amm}}+[AMM]}    [code: algebraic, computes \mu_{d}, code proposes constitutive]
    where

Symbols:
  X_{V}: viable cell density [10^9 cells L^{-1}] (computed)
  \mu: specific cell growth rate [h^{-1}] (computed)
  \mu_{d}: specific cell death rate [h^{-1}] (computed)
  [GLC]: glucose concentration [mM] (computed)
  Y_{X_V/glc}: biomass yield coefficient on glucose [10^9 cells mmol^{-1}] (parameter)
  m_{glc}: glucose maintenance coefficient [10^{-9} mmol cell^{-1} h^{-1}] (parameter)
  [GLN]: glutamine concentration [mM] (computed)
  Y_{X_V/g\ln}: biomass yield coefficient on glutamine [10^9 cells mmol^{-1}] (parameter)
  m_{g\ln}: glutamine maintenance coefficient [10^{-9} mmol cell^{-1} h^{-1}] (parameter)
  d_{g\ln}: first-order decomposition rate of glutamine [h^{-1}] (parameter)
  [LAC]: lactate concentration [mM] (computed)
  Y_{lac/glc}: lactate yield from glucose [mol mol^{-1}] (parameter)
  [AMM]: ammonia concentration [mM] (computed)
  Y_{amm/g\ln}: ammonia yield from glutamine [mol mol^{-1}] (parameter)
  r_{amm}: ammonia removal rate [10^{-9} mmol cell^{-1} h^{-1}] (parameter)
  [B1]: B1 protein titer (computed)
  Q_{B1}: specific B1 production rate [10^{-9} L cell^{-1} h^{-1}] (parameter)
  \mu_{\max}: maximum specific cell growth rate [h^{-1}] (parameter)
  K_{glc}: half-maximum-rate concentration of glucose for cell growth rate [mM] (parameter)
  K_{g\ln}: half-maximum-rate concentration of glutamine for cell growth rate [mM] (parameter)
  K: Substrate saturation constant in the growth-rate equation. [mM] (parameter)
  I_{lac}: Lactate inhibition constant in the growth-rate equation. [mM] (parameter)
  I_{amm}: Ammonia inhibition constant in the growth-rate equation. [mM] (parameter)
  k_{d}: Maximum cell death rate. [h^-1] (parameter)
  D_{lac}: Lactate saturation constant in the cell-death-rate equation. [mM] (parameter)
  D_{amm}: Ammonia saturation constant in the cell-death-rate equation. [mM] (parameter)

Model-wide assumptions (already recorded, do not repeat):
  - Specific growth rate is zero during the cell death phase.
  - Glucose and glutamine maintenance terms are zero when d ≤ 6.
  - Ammonia and lactate are considered in the growth-rate equation only above 90% of their thresholds.
  - The B1 mass balance is applied only after 144 h.

laws.description: Viable cell density changes through cell growth minus cell death.
laws.law_type_reason: The equation gives viable-cell accumulation as net growth and death.

laws.description: Glucose concentration decreases through growth-associated and maintenance consumption by viable cells.
laws.law_type_reason: The equation gives glucose accumulation from cellular consumption terms.

laws.description: Glutamine concentration decreases through cellular consumption and first-order decomposition.
laws.law_type_reason: The equation accounts for glutamine accumulation through consumption and decomposition.

laws.description: Lactate concentration increases according to a yield from glucose consumption.
laws.law_type_reason: The equation gives lactate accumulation from its production term.

laws.description: Ammonia concentration changes through glutamine-associated production and cellular removal.
laws.law_type_reason: The equation accounts for ammonia accumulation from production and removal terms.

laws.description: B1 titer accumulation is proportional to viable cell density and the estimated fraction of viable cells not propagating.
laws.quote: The mass balance for titer, [B1], was applied only after 144 h, as earlier samples are typically below the concentration range for the assay. In addition, since the highest specific antibody production rate was observed in the G1 or G0-phase of the cell cycle based on literature reports,²,⁴,²¹ the fraction of arrested viable cells was introduced into the mass balance equation for [B1].
laws.law_type_reason: The equation gives the accumulation of B1 titer through a production term.

laws.description: Specific growth rate increases with glucose and glutamine availability and is inhibited by lactate and ammonia.
laws.quote: inhibition to cell growth became significant when ammonia and/or lactate reached concentrations of 5.1 and 58 mM, respectively (threshold values).
laws.law_type_reason: The equation specifies the kinetic relationship for specific cell growth rate.

laws.description: Specific cell death rate increases with lactate and ammonia according to saturating terms.
laws.law_type_reason: The equation specifies the kinetic relationship for specific cell death rate.
